author: ZackyLake
title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails with PowerShell execution policy error before running tests
signature: windows gpu unit tests extract openvino packages setupvars.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system pssecurityexception unauthorizedaccess|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step failed with PSSecurityException/UnauthorizedAccess when PowerShell tried to dot-source a generated .ps1 wrapper script because script execution is disabled on the self-hosted Windows runner.

failed_jobs.name: JS API (24)
failed_jobs.symptom: tests/setup.js crashed with an unhandled promise rejection after the v3-small_224 model .bin download from storage.openvinotoolkit.org failed with 'read ECONNRESET', a transient TCP reset unrelated to the PR.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status-check job that runs `exit 1` because upstream jobs in the Windows pipeline failed; not an independent failure.

key_errors: . : File C:\actions-runner\_work\_temp\b15e0891-4697-4e57-af04-be745dfa17b1.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system. For more information, see about_Execution_Policies at https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=135170.
Failed to download the model: Failed to send request: Error: read ECONNRESET..

UnhandledPromiseRejection: This error originated either by throwing inside of an async function without a catch block, or by rejecting a promise which was not handled with .catch(). The promise rejected with the reason "Failed to send request: Error: read ECONNRESET.".
root_cause: The dominant, recurring failure is the 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step on the 'GPU unit tests' job, which runs under `shell: powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1). GitHub Actions implements this step by writing its `run:` block to a generated temporary .ps1 file under _temp and dot-sourcing it; on this self-hosted Windows runner the PowerShell execution policy for the Actions runner service account is Restricted (or was reset by a runner/image update or group policy refresh), which blocks loading any unsigned script file including the runner's own auto-generated wrapper. This is an environment/runner configuration issue on the self-hosted machine, not a problem introduced by commit d07632e9530196158b0714c659f1e97aff5490ea (#39839, GPU plugin shape-infer event generation), which does not touch Windows CI configuration. This is the 4th recorded occurrence of this exact PSSecurityException signature, indicating the execution-policy drift on this runner pool has not been remediated. Separately, the 'JS API (24)' job failed because tests/setup.js downloading v3-small_224_1.0_float.bin from storage.openvinotoolkit.org hit a TCP connection reset ('read ECONNRESET'); as with the earlier raw/media.githubusercontent.com timeout variants (patterns 6519f63a719d4f66, 49e48b464b80bcb7), the download promise's rejection is not wrapped in try/catch, so Node.js crashes the whole test run with an unhandled promise rejection instead of failing gracefully or retrying. This is reported as context but the PowerShell execution-policy issue is tracked as the primary signature for this investigation given its higher recurrence count and infrastructure-blocking nature.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires the specific self-hosted Windows GPU runner whose PowerShell execution policy is restricted. Locally: run `Set-ExecutionPolicy Restricted -Scope Process` then invoke any `shell: powershell` step to reproduce the PSSecurityException. For the JS API ECONNRESET: cd src/bindings/js/node && npm run test_setup repeatedly, or with a throttled/reset network route to storage.openvinotoolkit.org, to reproduce the connection reset.
recommended_actions: On the affected self-hosted Windows GPU runner(s), run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force` for the account running the Actions runner service, then verify with `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List`.

Audit whether a recent base-image update, group policy push, or security hardening script keeps resetting the execution policy on this runner pool (4th occurrence), and bake the required policy into the runner provisioning/imaging script so it survives reimaging or policy refreshes.

Add a runner startup health-check step that verifies `Get-ExecutionPolicy` before accepting GPU unit test workloads, failing fast with a clear diagnostic instead of a late PSSecurityException mid-pipeline.

Wrap all three model download calls in src/bindings/js/node/tests/setup.js in try/catch (or add .catch handlers) with retry/backoff so a transient ECONNRESET produces a clear test failure/retry instead of an unhandled promise rejection crash.
Consider caching the JS API test model artifacts (e.g., via actions/cache) to reduce dependence on live network access to storage.openvinotoolkit.org on every run.
prevention_strategies: Bake the required PowerShell execution policy into the Windows GPU runner image/provisioning script and add a pre-flight health check that fails fast with a clear diagnostic if the policy drifts. Separately, add network-call resiliency (timeout + retry + explicit error handling) to any CI step that downloads external resources at test time, including the JS API test setup script, and prefer committing/caching small fixed test assets instead of fetching them from remote hosts on every run.
historical_context: The PowerShell execution-policy signature (hash 3be0e72d6ae29098) has now recurred 4 times in under 24 hours (runs 43883526619, 43906839059, 44059103925, and this run 44068555035), confirming the runner-pool configuration drift has not been fixed. The JS API model-download-crash failure pattern has two prior sibling signatures for raw.githubusercontent.com (6519f63a719d4f66, count 2) and media.githubusercontent.com (49e48b464b80bcb7, count 1) timeouts; this run's storage.openvinotoolkit.org ECONNRESET is a related but distinct host/error combination and is noted as secondary context rather than updating a new pattern file, consistent with this investigation's focus on the dominant blocking signature.
